Article Title: India draws record $127 billion through forex deposits: RBI
Article Text:
Also read:

India mobilised a record $127.23 billion through foreign-currency deposits under a special central bank programme aimed at strengthening the country’s foreign-exchange liquidity, highlighting the role of the overseas Indian community in supporting the economy during periods of market stress, the Reserve Bank of India said on Wednesday.Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank), or FCNR(B), deposits accounted for $127.226 billion in inflows as of August 31, the RBI said.Including overseas foreign-currency borrowings (OFCB) and external commercial borrowings (ECB), total inflows under the measures stood at $136.377 billion.The strong response prompted the RBI to close the FCNR(B) window a month ahead of schedule. The facility, launched on June 8, was originally scheduled to remain open until September 30 but was closed on August 31 after the central bank said its objective had been achieved ahead of schedule.FCNR(B) deposits are fixed-term deposits held in foreign currencies, with the principal and interest repaid in the same currency. This allows non-resident Indians to park foreign-currency funds with Indian banks without taking direct exposure to rupee exchange-rate fluctuations.The inflows give Indian banks and the RBI a larger pool of foreign currency to manage external pressures and support liquidity in the foreign-exchange market, particularly during periods of heightened rupee volatility.The RBI did not provide bank-wise mobilisation figures. However, private-sector lender ICICI Bank said separately that it had mobilised $17.88 billion through FCNR(B) deposits up to August 31.Loans provided by the bank’s international branches and subsidiaries against such deposits stood at $9 billion, while standby letters of credit issued to other banks against loans backed by the deposits amounted to $3.63 billion.The RBI measures included absorbing hedging costs for banks mobilising FCNR(B) deposits and allowing banks to lend against the funds. The initiative was aimed at strengthening India’s external-sector position and improving foreign-exchange liquidity amid global uncertainty.Overseas foreign-currency borrowings contributed another $5.26 billion, while external commercial borrowings brought in $3.891 billion, according to provisional RBI data.The latest mobilisation is reminiscent of India’s response to the 2013 “taper tantrum”, when the RBI introduced a special FCNR(B) swap scheme to attract foreign-currency deposits from overseas Indians as the rupee came under severe pressure following the US Federal Reserve’s plans to reduce its monetary stimulus.The 2013 scheme mobilised around $26 billion in nearly three months and was followed by a sharp recovery in the rupee. Foreign-currency assets received through the latest swaps will be reflected as foreign-currency assets on the RBI’s balance sheet, potentially adding to the country’s foreign-exchange reserves.India’s forex reserves rose by $12.422 billion to a record $729.328 billion in the week ended August 21, according to the latest RBI data.The finance ministry said last week that the large-scale mobilisation of long-term non-resident deposits and institutional funding would strengthen India’s external buffers while providing foreign-currency resources to banks and companies, news agency PTI reported.It also said the response reflected the continuing role of the Indian diaspora in supporting India’s financial and economic growth and confidence in the resilience of the Indian economy and banking system.The record inflows came as India’s economy showed resilience despite heightened global uncertainty. GDP grew 7.8% in the April-June quarter, beating expectations and the RBI’s 7% forecast for the period.
Article Summary: Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) deposits accounted for $127.226 billion in inflows as of August 31. Total inflows under the measures stood at $136.377 billion. The strong response prompted the RBI to close the FCNR(B) window a month ahead of schedule.

Article Title: Oil price today: Crude continues to trade beyond $95 per barrel amid Hormuz supply tensions
Article Text:
Oil price today

Trump says US ready for further attacks

Global supply efforts continue

Oil prices edged lower on Thursday after a volatile session, as investors assessed the latest US-Iran strikes and their impact on oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.Brent crude stood at $95.33 a barrel, down 30 cents or 0.31% while WTI or West Texas Intermediate was trading at $90.88 a barrel, down 13 cents or 0.14%, around 7:30 am IST.This comes after both benchmarks saw sharp swings over the previous session, rising by as much as $2 a barrel before falling by up to $1. Their session highs were the highest since July 24, while Brent eventually settled 1% higher.A key focus for the market remained the Strait of Hormuz, where shipping activity has stayed below its usual level. Four commodity vessels transited the waterway on Wednesday, compared with a 10-day average of around 13, according to preliminary shipping data from Kpler, cited by Reuters.The waterway has effectively seen shipping traffic shut down since the war began with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iranian targets in late February. Before the conflict, the strait carried about a fifth of global oil and LNG consumed.The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said the latest US attacks would further restrict traffic through the strait. Iran has also added more ships to the list of vessels it considers non-compliant and subject to fines, confiscation or detention if they attempt to sail through the waterway.Two oil tankers were hit by sea mines and disabled while attempting to transit the strait, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Wednesday in a statement shared by state media.The latest escalation has come in the seventh month of the US-Iran war, with the latest attacks marking the biggest exchange of fire between Tehran and Washington since July.US forces struck Iran's southern coast, while Iran fired on American bases across the region.US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that the renewed US campaign against Iran would not continue for "too long". He also said US forces had targeted Iran's radar and missile systems."We took out all of the new equipment that they tried to build along the ‌Strait ⁠of Hormuz - some defensive, some offensive ... It was a very heavy attack last night, and we're prepared to do another one any time we want," Trump said.Despite the restrictions on traffic, the US said 17 million barrels of oil transited the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. It described this as the largest volume of crude to pass through the waterway since the US-Israeli war on Iran began.The disruption to shipping has raised concerns over world oil supplies, prompting nations worldwide to try to limit price rises by finding alternative sources of supply and relying on their reserves.Those reserves have also dwindled.The latest attacks have added another layer of uncertainty for oil markets already facing restricted movement through the Strait of Hormuz. Prices remained highly volatile during Wednesday's trading, with both Brent and WTI repeatedly moving between gains and losses before Brent ended the session higher.On Thursday, however, both benchmarks moved lower as investors assessed the uncertainty surrounding further military strikes and the potential disruption to supplies from the Middle East.
Article Summary: Brent crude was trading at $95.33 a barrel on Thursday, down 30 cents or 0.31%. WTI or West Texas Intermediate was at $90.88 a barrel, down 13 cents or0.14%. Both benchmarks saw sharp swings over the previous session, rising by as much as $2 a barrel.

Article Title: Rupee gains 47 paise as record FCNR inflows boost forex liquidity
Article Text:
Rupee gains 47 paise as record FCNR inflows boost forex liquidity (Image credit: Reuters)

Record FCNR(B) inflows strengthen RBI's hand

Dollar, oil prices remain in focus

Rupee began Thursday on a strong note, gaining 47 paise to 94.26 against US dollar in early trade, as record foreign-currency deposit mobilisation bolstered the country’s foreign-exchange liquidity.The currency opened at 94.30 at the interbank foreign exchange market before moving up to 94.26. It had closed at 94.73 on Wednesday, after gaining 22 paise.The strong move came after the Reserve Bank of India said foreign currency non-resident (Bank), or FCNR(B) deposits had brought in $127.226 billion as of August 31 under a special programme.Including overseas foreign-currency borrowings (OFCB) and external commercial borrowings (ECB), the measures attracted total inflows of $136.377 billion.Forex traders said that rupee was being supported by strong underlying inflows and aggressive intervention by the RBI, helping counter pressure from higher crude oil prices and global yields.The record mobilisation through FCNR(B) deposits has also raised the amount of liquidity that could enter the banking system as banks swap the deposits with the RBI."This gives RBI a long rope in terms of defending rupee, it creates a huge sterilisation problem as banking system liquidity surplus will likely go to around Rs 10 lakh crore as banks swap the deposits with RBI,” IFA Global said in a research note.The FCNR(B) deposits were mobilised under the special central-bank programme aimed at bolstering India's foreign-exchange liquidity.The dollar index was at 99.43, down 0.16 per cent. The index tracks the greenback against a basket of six major currencies. Its movement came amid safe-haven demand linked to renewed US-Iran tensions.Brent crude, meanwhile, was trading 0.16 per cent lower at $95.48 per barrel in futures trade. Oil prices were influenced by escalating US-Iran tensions and fears of disruption to flows through the Strait of Hormuz.Despite these pressures, rupee strengthened in early trading as the inflows and RBI intervention provided support.Domestic equities also opened higher with the BSE Sensex rising 221.17 points to 76,791.52, while Nifty gained 59.55 points to trade at 23,974.Foreign institutional investors were net buyers of Indian equities on Wednesday, purchasing shares worth Rs 6,688.37 crore, according to exchange data.
Article Summary: Rupee gains 47 paise to 94.26 against US dollar in early trade. Currency opened at 94.30 at the interbank foreign exchange market. Reserve Bank of India said foreign currency non-resident (Bank) deposits had brought in $127.226 billion as of August 31.

Article Title: A couple sold gold for Rs 20 lakh to buy a home, another family got Rs 80 lakh for a US degree and business: How Indians are unlocking value of idle gold sitting in their lockers
Article Text:
For many Indians these days, the real value of gold may lie not in keeping it locked away, but in unlocking it.

Gold jewellery value being unlocked

Gold price rise

They say old is gold, and indeed old gold is turning into a golden opportunity for families in India as prices of the yellow metal rise, yielding an asset that is now increasingly being used to meet goals.Take the case of Patils (name changed): a pair of heavy gold bangles, a bridal necklace and other heirloom jewellery had been inside their bank locker in Mumbai. And, while the pieces carried memories, for the couple they had little practical value in their daily lives.Then the couple, both in their late 20s, decided to sell this inherited gold. It was an emotional choice, but they had a bigger goal in mind: buying their first home in Navi Mumbai.The gold jewellery fetched them nearly Rs 20 lakh, which helped strengthen the couple’s down payment. The decision also had an immediate financial impact. Their monthly home loan instalment fell by around Rs 20,000, leaving them with more disposable income. They now use some of that money for weekend trips to Lonavala every alternate month.And, they are not alone. The Patils are part of a wider shift among younger Indians, who are increasingly looking at inherited gold not simply as jewellery to be preserved, but as an asset that can be used to finance major life goals.“Younger generations are driven by milestones. For them, old jewellery is no longer an emotional burden they feel compelled to hold on to for life,” Keyur Shah, CEO of Muthoot Exim, a gold recycling company, told ET.For some this trend means selling old ornaments to buy a home. For others, the money is being used to finance needs and goals such as higher education, a business or financial investments. Some are choosing a middle path, exchanging traditional jewellery for newer designs that fit their lifestyles better.Rajiv Popley, director of the Popley Group, says inherited gold is increasingly being recycled without the hesitation that once surrounded such decisions. At Popley outlets, old jewellery has become such an important part of the business that stores have effectively turned into scrap-buying centres, evaluating the purity of old ornaments and sending them through the recycling process.He estimates that more than 1 lakh tonnes of gold are lying idle in Indian lockers, with only a fraction having been recycled.Another young consumer in Bengaluru has taken a different route. A 25-year-old banker decided to sell her inherited jewellery after domestic gold prices surged and invest the proceeds in a diversified equity portfolio.Tannishtha Arora, a 31-year-old doctor in Delhi, sees little reason to keep jewellery locked away simply because it has been passed down through generations.“Jewellery passed down from our mothers and grandmothers is often too heavy and dated in design to be worn daily. If it’s only going to sit in a locker as an investment, it might as well be converted into gold bars or coins,” she told ET.For one Bengaluru family, the decision involved three generations. A 24-year-old, his parents and grandparents agreed to sell part of their idle gold jewellery, raising nearly Rs 80 lakh. Some of the money paid for his master’s degree in the US, while another portion became seed capital for his father’s new food processing business.Behind these individual decisions is a sharp rise in gold prices. Domestic gold prices crossed Rs 160,000 for 10 grams earlier this year before moderating in recent months. Gold prices rose 33% year-on-year in FY2025 and surged 60% in FY2026.The high prices are also changing what Indians buy. ICRA’s analysis, based on data from the Gold Council of India, shows that gold jewellery demand by volume fell 21% year-on-year in FY2026, while demand for bars and coins rose about 22%.That divergence suggests that gold is increasingly being treated as an investment rather than simply an ornament, particularly by younger consumers.Ajay Srivastava, founder of Delhi-based trade think tank GTRI, says elevated prices are encouraging households to sell or exchange old jewellery. Jewellery chains are also expanding recycling and exchange programmes, partly reducing their need for fresh gold.Yet the emotional value of gold has not disappeared. And, there is another side to the recycling boom.ICRA expects India’s domestic jewellery industry to grow around 15% in value in the current financial year, driven by high gold prices and investment demand, even as jewellery consumption by volume is expected to decline again.What is changing is what a younger generation wants it to do with idle gold. For some, the jewellery in the locker is no longer something to preserve indefinitely. It can become a house, an education, a business or an investment.For them, the real value of gold may lie not in keeping it locked away, but in unlocking it.
Article Summary: Young Indians are increasingly looking at inherited gold not as jewellery to be preserved, but as an asset that can be used to finance major life goals. Domestic gold prices crossed Rs 160,000 for 10 grams earlier this year before moderating in recent months. More than 1 lakh tonnes of gold are lying idle in Indian lockers.

Article Title: Her son died in 2013, LIC rejected all 5 insurance claims saying he hid diabetes; 12 years later, Mumbai mother wins Rs 61.5 lakh plus 9% interest payout
Article Text:
The key issue in deciding the claims under the final two policies was the actual date on which LIC received the first premium.

What the LIC insurance payout dispute was about:

Family’s case

What the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission found

The dispute over the premium date

What LIC has been ordered to pay

Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) of India has been ordered to pay Rs 60 lakh cumulatively after a woman’s claim was rejected following her son’s death. The National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed LIC to pay more than Rs 60 lakh in life insurance proceeds to a Mumbai woman after concluding that the insurer had not been justified in repudiating all five policies purchased by her son, who died of cardiac arrest in 2013.The decision ends a legal dispute that continued for more than a decade. It also establishes that an insurer cannot deny a death claim for non-disclosure of a medical condition if the policyholder himself was unaware of the disease when the policy was taken.The case dates back to June 2010, when Nitin Suresh Gambhir, who lived in Mahim, Mumbai, submitted proposals to LIC for five life insurance policies. As part of the process, he underwent a medical examination by a doctor from LIC's own panel.Three of the policies commenced on 26 August 2010, with the risk also beginning on that date. Their respective sums assured were Rs 10 lakh, Rs 15 lakh and Rs 15 lakh.The other two policies carried a sum assured of Rs 10 lakh each. The family said that the first premium for these policies was paid on 7 September 2010. LIC subsequently maintained that it had received the first premium only on 13 September 2010 and, on that basis, treated that date as the commencement of risk.On 11 September 2010, the family said four days had passed since it paid the premium for the final two policies when Nitin was admitted to P.D. Hinduja National Hospital in Mumbai.He was hospitalized because of a wound on his right leg that had remained unhealed for 15 days.During the hospital stay, medical records described Nitin as a known diabetic for two months. The records also stated that he had been taking a hypoglycaemic agent. He received treatment and was discharged from the hospital on 13 September 2010.Almost three years later, on 11 June 2013, Nitin died following a cardiac arrest.Following Nitin’s death, his mother, Jayshree Suresh Gambhir, submitted claims under each of the five life insurance policies. LIC rejected all five claims in a repudiation letter issued on 11 July 2014, according to an ET report.The insurer alleged that Nitin had failed to disclose important information about his health while filling out the proposal form. LIC relied on the discharge summary issued by Hinduja Hospital, which recorded that Nitin had been diabetic for two months as of September 2010. On this basis, the insurer contended that the disease must have been present around June 2010, when the insurance proposals were submitted.LIC further pointed out that Nitin had answered “no” to questions in the proposal form relating to diabetes and previous hospitalisation. The insurer argued that this amounted to a breach of the principle of utmost good faith and rendered the policies void.Jayshree then took the matter to the Maharashtra State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. After reviewing the documents and the relevant dates, the state commission treated the five policies differently.In the case of the first three policies, the commission noted that the risk had begun on 26 August 2010. Nitin’s hospitalisation, meanwhile, took place on 11 September 2010, meaning he was admitted only after these policies had already come into force. The commission therefore allowed the claims relating to these three policies.The position was different for the remaining two policies. The state commission accepted LIC’s contention that the first premium for these policies had been received on 13 September 2010, the date on which Nitin was discharged from the hospital.As the hospitalisation occurred during the period between the premium payment and the commencement of risk, the state commission agreed with LIC’s decision to reject the claims under these two policies.Neither side accepted the outcome. LIC challenged the state commission’s decision allowing the claims under the first three policies, while Jayshree appealed against the rejection of the remaining two.Both appeals subsequently came before the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.The bench, headed by Presiding Member Dr. Inderjit Singh and Member Shashi Nandkeolyar, reviewed the matter from the outset and ultimately ruled in favour of the family on all five policies.On the question of whether Nitin had failed to disclose his diabetes, the commission found that LIC had not produced any medical records establishing that he was suffering from diabetes, or even knew that he had the condition, before signing the proposal form on 27 June 2010.Although the September 2010 hospital discharge summary stated that he had been diabetic for two months, the commission held that this reference by itself could not establish that Nitin was aware of the disease when he completed the proposal form.The commission also considered another medical record from February 2013, only a few months before Nitin died. That record described him as non-diabetic, further weakening LIC's argument regarding the alleged non-disclosure.The commission also examined the circumstances surrounding Nitin's death. He died from cardiac arrest in June 2013, almost three years after he had been hospitalised for the leg wound. According to the commission, there was no connection established between the cellulitis in his leg and the cardiac arrest. LIC had also failed to establish such a link.The key issue in deciding the claims under the final two policies was the actual date on which LIC received the first premium.LIC relied on two documents described as First Premium Receipts, both carrying the date 13 September 2010. The commission, however, observed that these receipts did not establish the date on which LIC actually received the premium. They only showed the date on which the receipts were issued.Jayshree, on the other hand, submitted two Proposal Deposit Receipts, both dated 7 September 2010. These documents specifically recorded that Rs 40,100 had been received as premium in each case.After comparing the documents, the commission considered the Proposal Deposit Receipts more reliable. It concluded that LIC had received the first premium for both policies on 7 September 2010, four days before Nitin was admitted to hospital.The proposal form required the policyholder to inform LIC about any adverse change in health occurring between submission of the proposal and receipt of the first premium. Since the first premium had already been received before Nitin's hospitalisation in the case of all five policies, the commission held that he was not required to provide such information for any of them.The national commission therefore agreed with the state commission's decision to allow the claims under the first three policies, but found that the state commission had erred in rejecting the claims relating to the other two.LIC has been ordered to pay Rs 60 lakh towards the sum assured under all five policies. This includes Rs 10 lakh under each of three policies and Rs 15 lakh under each of the remaining two.The Rs 1 lakh compensation awarded by the state commission for mental agony has also been upheld. In addition, total litigation costs have been fixed at Rs 50,000. This takes the total payout ordered to Rs 61.5 lakh, before the applicable interest.Interest will be payable on all these amounts at 9 per cent per annum from the date LIC repudiated the claims in July 2014 until the payment is made in full.
Article Summary: The case dates back to June 2010, when Nitin Suresh Gambhir, who lived in Mahim, Mumbai, submitted proposals to LIC for five life insurance policies. The key issue in deciding the claims under the final two policies was the actual date on which LIC received the first premium.

Article Title: BCCL's Mohit Jain elected chairman of Audit Bureau of Circulations
Article Text:
A file photo of Mohit Jain

MUMBAI: Mohit Jain, chief operating officer, publishing, and board member of Bennett, Coleman & Co (BCCL), has been unanimously elected chairman of the Audit Bureau of Circulations (ABC) for 2026-27. The Economic Times is published by BCCL.The ABC is a grouping that comprises publishers, advertisers and advertising agencies. It conducts market surveys and certifies circulation figures reported by publishers.Jain’s election marks BCCL’s return to the chairmanship of the ABC after 43 years since its previous representative held the position.Taking charge as chairman, Jain said the focus will be on furthering newspaper readership.“To engage younger and urban households, newspapers are innovating in content, design, distribution and their integration with digital platforms,” Jain said. “Publishers are also using campaigns to reinforce the value of a daily reading habit—depth, perspective, discovery and trusted information. The objective is not merely to preserve circulation, but to make newspapers relevant and indispensable to a new generation of readers.Jain has more than two decades of experience in the print media industry and has held senior leadership positions in publishing, business operations and industry affairs. He brings to the ABC extensive sectoral experience and an understanding of issues shaping the future of print media, circulation and publishing.
Article Summary: Mohit Jain has been unanimously elected chairman of the Audit Bureau of Circulations. The Economic Times is published by Bennett, Coleman & Co (BCCL) Jain said the focus will be on furthering newspaper readership. He has more than two decades of experience in the print media industry.

Article Title: Tata Sons clears 10k crore for Air India, with conditions attached
Article Text:
The people said the ban does not affect voting rights of Tata Trusts’ nominee directors. Nominee directors, appointed under article 104B, owe their primary fiduciary duty to Tata Sons, and their voting rights under article 121A remain intact unless they resign or are formally removed.

MUMBAI: Tata Sons’ board has cleared a fresh capital infusion of over Rs 10,000 crore (about $1.1 billion) into Air India, one of its largest commitments to the airline since the Rs 18,000-crore acquisition in 2021, though the approval comes with conditions, people familiar with the matter said.The decision was taken at a June board meeting chaired by N Chandrasekaran and attended by Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata and vice-chairman Venu Srinivasan. Under Article 121A of Tata Sons’ articles of association, investments above Rs 100 crore require majority backing from Tata Trusts’ nominee directors.The board granted in-principle approval for fresh investment in Air India and other group ventures, subject to conditions, the people said. “Any capital infusion will require Air India and other investee companies to present a business case when funding is sought,” one person said.The approval comes more than a year after Tata Sons paused equity injections into Air India, whose losses more than doubled to Rs 22,238 crore in FY26. The losses were among the key issues that drove a rift between Noel and Chandrasekaran, culminating in the latter’s Aug announcement that he will step down when his term ends in Feb 2027.Tata Sons’ board is due to meet on Sept 17, a week after Tata Trusts, excluding Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT), meets on Sept 11. SRTT has been barred from holding board meetings since May, pending an inquiry into alleged violations of the Maharashtra Public Trusts Act.The people said the ban does not affect voting rights of Tata Trusts’ nominee directors. Nominee directors, appointed under article 104B, owe their primary fiduciary duty to Tata Sons, and their voting rights under article 121A remain intact unless they resign or are formally removed.Tata Sons’ FY26 report showed its investment in Air India unchanged at Rs 22,618 crore, indicating no fresh equity was injected during the year. The airline relied on borrowings and other financing, pushing outstanding debt to about Rs 40,000 crore across 11 lenders. State Bank of India has the largest exposure at Rs 18,500 crore, followed by Bank of Baroda at Rs 5,938 crore.Tata Sons’ ability to backstop those lenders is also constrained by its decision to stop issuing corporate guarantees or letters of comfort while its application to surrender its core investment company registration awaits RBI approval.Tata Sons owns 73.8% of Air India, employees hold about 1.5% through SBICAP Trustee Co and Singapore Airlines holds 24.7%. To avoid any dilution, SIA would need to invest about Rs 3,350 crore ($351 million) to maintain its stake.Tata Sons and Tata Trusts both declined to comment.
Article Summary: The decision was taken at a June board meeting chaired by N Chandrasekaran. Under Article 121A of Tata Sons’ articles of association, investments above Rs 100 crore require majority backing from Tata Trusts’ nominee directors. The board granted in-principle approval for fresh investment in Air India and other group ventures, subject to conditions.

Article Title: Canada fund buys 24% in tower firm for $1.3bn
Article Text:
Canada’s La Caisse (formerly CDPQ) has bought a 24% stake in Brookfield-backed Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust

MUMBAI: Canada’s La Caisse (formerly CDPQ) has bought a 24% stake in Brookfield-backed Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust for about Rs 12,100 crore ($1.3 billion). Brookfield and its entities will remain the largest shareholder in the company with a 37% stake.Affiliates of GIC and British Columbia Investment Management Corporation (BCI) are the other shareholders of Altius which owns and operates more than 2,58,000 telecom towers and sites across India.“As India’s economy grows and more people and businesses rely on higher use of mobile data, the infrastructure behind those connections needs to keep pace,” said Emmanuel Jaclot, executive vice-president and head of infrastructure and sustainability at La Caisse. Altius provides the infrastructure that enables mobile operators to deliver 4G and 5G services. India is the world’s second-largest telecommunications market, and continued growth in mobile data use and 5G is increasing the need for digital infrastructure.The deal comes ahead of Altius’ planned IPO which could raise about Rs 6,000 crore and transition from a privately listed infrastructure investment trust (InvIT) to a publicly listed InvIT.Last month, the company filed draft IPO papers with markets regulator Sebi.Initially operating as Data Infrastructure Trust (DIT), it was rebranded as Altius in 2024 following the acquisition of American Tower’s (ATC) operations in India by a Brookfield-led consortium.“Altius has built a scaled, nationwide platform that is in a leading position to meet India’s demand for mobile connectivity and 5G infrastructure. La Caisse’s investment brings another long-term institutional partner to the platform and reflects confidence in the strength of the business,” said Sam Pollock, CEO at Brookfield’s Infrastructure group. “Alongside our partners, we will continue to support Altius’ next phase of growth. ”Telecom tower companies are poised for growth in tenancy this fiscal and the next, driven by continued capital expenditure by telcos, analysts at Crisil said in a June report.Additionally, revival in capex by select telcos, particularly in overlapping circles, will translate to incremental tenancies at existing tower sites, leading to improvement in the tenancy ratio in this fiscal and the next, after years of moderation.
Article Summary: Canada’s La Caisse (formerly CDPQ) has bought a 24% stake in Brookfield-backed Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust. Brookfield and its entities will remain the largest shareholder in the company with a 37% stake. Altius owns and operates more than 2,58,000 telecom towers and sites across India.

Article Title: High-value tech imports a worry: Auto cos
Article Text:
India’s auto industry is warning that its next big vulnerability may not be vehicle production, but dependence on imported high-value technologies

New Delhi: India’s auto industry is warning that its next big vulnerability may not be vehicle production, but dependence on imported high-value technologies, with the chiefs of Hyundai Motor India and Maruti Suzuki calling for deeper localisation across semiconductors, battery cells, power electronics and other critical components.At ACMA’s annual session, Hyundai Motor India MD & CEO Tarun Garg said India exported about $24 billion worth of auto components in 2025-26, but imported around $25.4 billion, resulting in a $1.4-billion trade deficit. “The concern goes beyond the deficit. Our exports remain concentrated in relatively mature technologies, while our imports are led by advanced, higher-value technologies, which may well define the future,” he said.Garg said the industry needs to build domestic capability in semiconductor chips, rare-earth magnets, power electronics and battery cells, while stepping up investments in R&D and intellectual property. “Technology ownership is essential for strategic independence,” he said, adding that India must progress from exporting conventional components to advanced technologies and engineering capability.Maruti Suzuki India MD & CEO Hisashi Takeuchi also identified “deep localisation” as critical to insulating the industry from global disruptions.“Deep localisation is about reducing our exposure to external disruptions by strengthening domestic capabilities and progressively owning a larger share of the value chain,” he said.Takeuchi said changing global supply chains, govt support and India’s expanding automotive scale were creating a stronger case for localisation. Rising domestic demand and export opportunities, he said, now justify investments “including advanced technologies that were previously considered difficult to manufacture competitively in India.”Both executives also stressed that localisation would have to extend beyond large OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers. Takeuchi said stronger technology, engineering and quality capabilities among Tier-2 and Tier-3 suppliers would be critical, while Garg called for digitalisation, AI and shared learning to spread across the wider supplier ecosystem.
Article Summary: India’s auto industry is warning that its next big vulnerability may not be vehicle production, but dependence on imported high-value technologies. The chiefs of Hyundai Motor India and Maruti Suzuki call for deeper localisation across semiconductors, battery cells, power electronics and other critical components.

Article Title: Fresh investments by pvt cos jump 97% in Q1: CMIE
Article Text:
India’s private sector announced fresh investment projects worth Rs 15.4 lakh core

NEW DELHI: Defying expectations, India’s private sector announced fresh investment projects worth Rs 15.4 lakh core in April-June quarter (Q1), a 97% jump compared to corresponding quarter of the previous financial year, latest CMIE data showed. This improvement in confidence was led by fresh investments in the electricity and services sectors, particularly in the IT segment.Overall, the fresh capex (govt and private) in the economy touched a five-quarter high of Rs 17.8 lakh crore, even as fresh govt capex during Q1 FY27 declined 36% to Rs 2.4 lakh crore from Rs 3.9 lakh crore in Q1 FY26.CMIE data showed new investments in the electricity and services sector in Q1 FY27 more than doubled to Rs 7.6 lakh crore from Rs 3.6 lakh crore and Rs 7.8 lakh crore from Rs 3.8 lakh crore respectively. In the services sector, new investments in IT sector alone rose nearly four times to Rs 6.5 lakh crore from Rs 1.6 lakh crore.Bank of Baroda chief economist Madan Sabnavis said share of capital formation in Q1 rose to 34.3% in nominal terms from 31.4% last year, with private capex “being driven by data centres and power.”IDFC First Bank chief economist Gaura Sengupta said nascent signs of a pick-up in private capex are visible, with a “rise in bank lending to the infrastructure sector, capital goods imports and capital goods production.”Fresh investments in the manufacturing sector, however, fell 40% to Rs 2.2 lakh crore from Rs 3.8 lakh crore, led by decline in investments in the food products industry, textiles, chemicals and construction materials. Construction sector also saw decline in investments to Rs 15,000 crore from Rs 40,900 crore. Data also showed that project completions remained nearly similar (Rs 2.4 lakh crore) in Q1 as compared to the corresponding quarter of the previous year, while projects worth Rs 1 lakh crore were abandoned or shelved during Q1 FY27.
Article Summary: India’s private sector announced fresh investment projects worth Rs 15.4 lakh core in April-June quarter. This improvement in confidence was led by fresh investments in the electricity and services sectors. Overall, the fresh capex (govt and private) in the economy touched a five-quarter high of Rs 17.8 lakh crore.

Article Title: Russia largest supplier of crude in Aug, US tops LPG, LNG volumes
Article Text:
Russia remained the largest supplier of crude to India in August

NEW DELHI: Russia remained the largest supplier of crude to India in Aug, while US supplied highest volumes of LPG and LNG, data from maritime intelligence and research firm Kpler shows.India purchased 2.1 million barrels of crude per day from Russia this month, accounting for 45% of its total oil imports. The figure, however, was down from 2.8 mbd in July, which was the highest ever. The other top suppliers included the UAE (0.5 mbd), Saudi Arabia (0.5 mbd) and Venezuela (0.3 mbd).India’s overall crude imports also declined in Aug compared with May, June and July, when refiners ramped up purchases to guard against any shortfall in a scenario of the conflict in West Asia escalating. Crude supplies in Aug were estimated at 4.6 mbd, nearly 8% lower than the over 5 mbd imported in July. Experts said the decline reflected some moderation after strong buying in recent months, scheduled maintenance at some refineries in India and lower availability of Russian crude.India also emerged as a key supplier of gasoline (petrol) and diesel to Russia as refinery operations in the country were hit by Ukrainian attacks on its facilities.According to energy analytics firm Vortexa, Russia’s seaborne gasoline imports increased to 125,000 barrels per day in Aug, equivalent to a projected 470,000 tonnes for the month, with the supplies coming from countries such as India, Türkiye and Morocco.US emerged as the largest supplier of LPG and LNG, accounting for nearly 51% and 38%, respectively, of India’s total imports during the month. Of the 1.1 million tonnes of LPG imported by India, about 0.6 MT of cooking and heating gas came from the US, compared with 0.9 MT in July. The UAE (0.1 MT) and Algeria (0.1 MT) were the other major suppliers.US also supplied 0.8 MT of the 2.2 MT of LNG imported by India during the month, followed by Oman (0.5 MT) and Nigeria (0.4 MT). The diversification of energy imports, however, has led to higher commodity costs due to increased freight bills from longer voyages and insurance charges, experts added.
Article Summary: India purchased 2.1 million barrels of crude per day from Russia this month, accounting for 45% of its total oil imports. The figure, however, was down from 2.8 mbd in July, which was the highest ever. India also emerged as key supplier of gasoline (petrol) and diesel to Russia.

Article Title: Govt defends GDP data after ex-FS claims Q1 growth 2.6%
Article Text:
Govt on Wednesday strongly defended the sanctity of GDP data

‘Going forward, no substantial revision in GDP no.s expected’

NEW DELHI: Govt on Wednesday strongly defended the sanctity of GDP data, and argued its critics' arguments are flawed. Critics pointed to the revision in nominal GDP number in Q1 FY 25-26, the base period for calculating this FY's QI growth rate. Govt said the revision was consistent with the new methodology. The base year has changed, the use of producer price index provides more granular information, and more data is available. This led to the revision, which is completely kosher, govt said.The statistics ministry said Q1 GDP estimate for 2025-26 was lowered from Rs 86 lakh crore to Rs 80 lakh crore as it was based on earlier series (2011-12 base year), which has now been updated to 2022-23.Former finance secretary Subhash Chandra Garg had said nominal GDP growth would have been about 2.6% during April-June 2026-27 and real GDP growth close to 0% if last year's GDP had not been revised down from Rs 86 lakh crore to Rs 80 lakh crore.The statistics ministry said Wednesday GDP numbers from different series cannot be compared to arrive at the growth rate.Accordingly, GDP at current prices under the new series was estimated at about Rs 80.3 lakh crore for June quarter of the last fiscal year.This was revised to Rs 80.4 lakh crore in June because of the availability and updation of indicators and data. As the new series of Index of Industrial Production (IIP) and PPI became available and were incorporated into the GDP compilation, the first quarter GDP at current prices for 2025-26 was revised to Rs 80 lakh crore, it said.On Monday, govt released growth figures for Q1 FY 2026-27 which also saw revisions in both the preceding quarterly and annual figures. For example, growth for Jan-March quarter of financial year 2025-26 was revised upwards to 8.6% from the provisional estimate of 7.8%. Similarly, annual growth in 2023-24 is now estimated to have been 7.3%, up from 7.2%, while a similar 10-basis-point (bps) upward revision has been made for 2024-25 and 2025-26 to 7.2% and 7.8%, respectively.On Wednesday, statistics secretary Saurabh Garg told reporters that quarterly estimates are largely based on indicators and are revised as more comprehensive information on corporate performance, govt activity and actual output becomes available, whereas annual figures are generally more robust.“There is no consistent upward or downward bias in the new series as some quarters had been revised higher and others lower,” he said.Going forward, no “substantial” revisions in GDP figures are anticipated, barring a few basis points, he added. “The earlier series relied on around 180 deflators, while the new methodology uses more than 300. The greater granularity allows to undertake double deflation more comprehensively across the manufacturing sector,” Garg told reporters.Under double deflation, output and the inputs used in production are deflated separately to arrive at real value added.
Article Summary: Critics pointed to the revision in nominal GDP number in Q1 FY 25-26. Govt said the revision was consistent with the new methodology. Former finance secretary Subhash Chandra Garg had said nominal GDP growth would have been about 2.6% during April-June 2026-27 and real GDP growth close to 0%.

Article Title: Speak up for Bengaluru tunnel road, DKS tells entrepreneurs
Article Text:
DK Shivakumar, chief minister of Karnataka

BENGALURU

: Chief minister D K Shivakumar on Wednesday urged women entrepreneurs to publicly support his government’s tunnel-road project, saying some political leaders were opposing the plan for political reasons even as Bengaluru’s traffic continued to worsen.Addressing the fifth edition of “Together We Grow,” organised by the Ubuntu Consortium at FKCCI, Shivakumar said the city’s mobility problems were costing businesses and workers both time and money. He asked the gathering to speak up about the issue and hold political leaders accountable.“Even, shout at me if I am doing wrong,” he said, adding that entrepreneurs had a direct stake in improving mobility because employees needed to travel to their establishments and factories.Shivakumar defended the tunnel-road proposal as a necessary response to Bengaluru’s constrained road network. He said widening existing roads was difficult because much of the city had not been planned for its present scale. Travelling from Mysuru to Bengaluru could take about 90 minutes, he said, but entering the city and reaching the final destination could take even longer.He reiterated that the government was investing more than Rs 1.5 lakh crore in Bengaluru’s development and mobility infrastructure.The city’s rapid growth and rising number of vehicles had made travel increasingly difficult, he said.The remarks come amid intensified opposition to the proposed north-south tunnel corridor between Hebbal and Silk Board. The project has faced criticism from the BJP, civic groups and urban-mobility experts. Critics have questioned its cost and argued that car-focused infrastructure could undermine the city’s public-transport goals.Concerns have also been raised over its possible impact on green spaces, particularly Lalbagh. The controversy sharpened after the state legislature passed amendments relating to the use of parkland for public infrastructure and the clearance of large urban-transport projects. Shivakumar has maintained that the tunnel would pass beneath Lalbagh without damaging the garden.At the event, the chief minister also assured women entrepreneurs of government support. He said running a business involved considerable financial stress, including meeting salaries, paying suppliers and servicing loans.“You are not employees. You are employers,” he said, praising women entrepreneurs for creating jobs and assuming a wider responsibility towards society.Shivakumar pointed to the state’s subsidised financing facility under which eligible women entrepreneurs can access Karnataka State Financial Corporation loans at an effective interest rate of 4%. He also called for more educated women to enter politics and assume leadership roles from gram panchayats to Parliament.The chief minister questioned the continued preference for sons in Indian families. Recalling the birth of his granddaughter on May 1, he said his wife had hoped the first grandchild would be a boy. Shivakumar said he had challenged that thinking, pointing to the success of their daughter Aishwarya.Referring to the Ramayana, he said Sita’s role was stronger than Rama’s, citing her sacrifices, struggles and resilience. He urged women entrepreneurs to remain confident and become partners in Karnataka’s growth.
Article Summary: Chief minister D K Shivakumar urged women entrepreneurs to publicly support his government’s tunnel-road project. He said some political leaders were opposing the plan for political reasons. The remarks come amid intensified opposition to the proposed north-south tunnel corridor between Hebbal and Silk Board.

Article Title: Simple Energy sees demand of up to 4,000 EVs a month, backlog at 2,200
Article Text:
Team Simple Energy

TOI

BENGALURU: IPO-bound Simple Energy estimates monthly demand at 3,000-4,000 scooters but is delivering around 1,500-2,000, leaving a rolling backlog of 2,000-2,200 vehicles, founder and CEO Shreshth Mishra told“Today, demand is not a problem for us. We have almost double the demand of what we are able to supply,” Mishra said. Customers are typically waiting about a month, he added.The company expects output to begin rising from the end of September or in October. Mishra said recently raised capital was being deployed to expand its manufacturing operations and supplier capacity.His comments came as Simple launched Wave, its first family-focused electric scooter. The lineup has six models across three variants, with battery packs ranging from 2.2kWh to 5kWh and claimed test-cycle ranges of 110km to 243km. Prices start at a little over Rs 1 lakh, while deliveries are scheduled to begin in the last week of September.The entry price applies to the base model. Simple has not disclosed the price of the 5kWh Wave+, which carries the headline 243km range. Mishra said the introductory price would remain for the “foreseeable future”, with detailed variant prices to be released separately.Wave uses the same motor, battery and chassis platform as Simple One, with modifications for a family-scooter layout. Mishra said this allowed the company to develop it faster while using components already tested on vehicles on the road.Simple currently describes its effective production capacity as 3,000 scooters a month. Mishra said the physical plant could make more, but output had been constrained by supplier capacity, the production ramp and the size of its dealership network.Simple has more than 75 exclusive outlets across over 60 cities and is targeting monthly sales of 10,000 scooters by March 2027. It has raised Rs 736 crore to date, including a recent Rs 250-crore debt-and-equity round.Asked about Wave’s Rs 10,000 premium over competitors, Mishra said Simple would compete on value rather than price alone. He said the 5kWh version is already the highest-selling configuration in Simple’s existing portfolio.
Article Summary: Simple Energy estimates monthly demand at 3,000-4,000 scooters but is delivering around 1,500-2,000. The company expects output to begin rising from the end of September or in October. Simple launched Wave, its first family-focused electric scooter.

Article Title: Teachers' Day 2026: Best speech ideas and quotes for students to use on September 5
Article Text:
Teachers' day 2026

The man who declined his own birthday

Speech topics that go beyond "thank you"

What Radhakrishnan actually meant by a teacher

Build the speech around his line that true teachers are those who help students think for themselves, and argue for what that looks like in a modern classroom.

The guru-shishya tradition, updated

Trace how the old idea of a teacher as a life guide, not just a subject expert, still shows up in today's schools and colleges.

One teacher, one turning point

A short, specific story about a single lesson or piece of advice from an actual teacher tends to land harder than any general tribute.

Teaching as nation building

Use Radhakrishnan's own belief that a country's character depends on the character of the people it educates.

The classroom in the age of artificial intelligence (AI)

Ask what a teacher offers that a screen or a chatbot cannot, and make the case for why that gap matters more, not less, as technology advances.

Why the best teachers ask questions instead of answering them

A speech built on Socratic method, tied back to Radhakrishnan's own line about ceasing to learn the moment we think we know.

The invisible curriculum

Focus on what teachers pass on that never appears on a syllabus: patience, discipline, curiosity, the willingness to be wrong in public.

Quotes worth building a speech around

"When we think we know, we cease to learn": Radhakrishnan's own words make a natural opening or closing line, particularly for a speech about intellectual humility.

"True teachers are those who help us think for ourselves."

"A teacher affects eternity; he can never tell where his influence stops": Written by the American historian Henry Adams in his 1907 memoir, this line works well for a speech about long term impact, the kind a teacher rarely gets to see play out.

"Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world": Nelson Mandela said this at Madison Park High School in Boston in 1990, and it remains one of the most reliably quoted lines on education worldwide, useful for a speech with a broader, global framing.

"The role of teachers has acquired new dimensions in the era of technology": President Droupadi Murmu's own Teachers' Day message is a useful, current line for any speech that wants to address how teaching is changing rather than only how it once was.

Closing the way Radhakrishnan might have

Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, a philosopher who twice served as Vice-Chancellor of an Indian university before he ever held political office, once said that when we think we know, we cease to learn. It is a strange thing for a man to say after becoming the second President of India, a position that tends to invite the opposite instinct, and it is stranger still that this same man responded to an offer of a birthday celebration by asking the country to celebrate teachers instead.That request is the reason September 5 exists on the Indian calendar as it does. In 2026, the date falls on a Saturday, and it marks the 65th year that India has observed Teachers' Day since Radhakrishnan first proposed it in 1962. For students expected to stand up and say something meaningful about their teachers this year, that origin story is worth understanding before the speech writing begins, because it changes the shape of what there is to say.When Radhakrishnan became President in 1962, a group of his former students asked for permission to mark his birthday with some ceremony. He turned the request around. Instead of celebrating him personally, he suggested the day be observed as Teachers' Day, in recognition of everyone who had ever stood in front of a classroom. India has kept that arrangement every year since, distinct from World Teachers' Day, which UNESCO and much of the rest of the world mark on October 5 instead.Radhakrishnan's own path to that classroom had been a long one. Born in Tiruttani in 1888, he studied philosophy at Madras Christian College and went on to serve as Vice-Chancellor of Andhra University and later Banaras Hindu University, publishing influential work including a study of Rabindranath Tagore's philosophy. He was nominated for the Nobel Prize in Literature multiple times and the Nobel Peace Prize eleven times over his career, and was awarded India's highest civilian honour, the Bharat Ratna, in 1954. In one of his essays, titled Character is Destiny, he argued that the purpose of education was never simply to produce technically skilled graduates, but to build people capable of compassion and democratic spirit. It is that essay, more than any policy speech, which explains why he thought teachers deserved a day more than presidents did.Most Teachers' Day speeches default to gratitude, and gratitude is not a bad place to start. But a speech built only on thanks tends to sound the same as every other one delivered that morning. These angles tend to hold an audience for longer.A speech does not need many quotes, but the right one at the right moment gives an audience something to hold on to. These are drawn from figures whose words on teaching are well documented and easy to verify, rather than the misattributed lines that circulate every September.A speech that opens by asking what a teacher really is tends to work best if it closes the same way. Radhakrishnan never wanted the day named after him in the first place, and the most memorable student speeches tend to follow his lead: less about performance, more about the specific person who changed how you thought. That is a harder speech to write than a list of thanks, but it is the one a room actually remembers.
Article Summary: 2026 marks the 65th year that India has observed Teachers' Day. Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan proposed the day in 1962. He argued that a country's character depends on the character of the people it educates.

Article Title: Raghav Chadha alleges AAP’s hand in marking his name ‘shifted’ in Punjab draft rolls; party hits back
Article Text:
Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha (L) And Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann

AAP rejects allegation

20.66 lakh names removed from draft roll

Key dates:

Claims and objections window | Aug 13 to Sept 12

Fill out Form 6 (for inclusion of names); young citizens turning eligible by the qualifying date of Oct 1, 2026, can also apply





CHANDIGARH: Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha has accused the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in Punjab of political vendetta after his name was marked as “shifted” in the state’s draft electoral roll.Chadha, who was elected to the Rajya Sabha as an AAP nominee in 2022 and joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) this year, raised the allegation in a post on X on Thursday.He claimed his voter ID was registered in Mohali and questioned why his name had been classified as “shifted” in the draft electoral roll."The AAP government in Punjab has now taken its politics of revenge to the Draft Electoral Rolls.I am a sitting Rajya Sabha MP from Punjab, with my voter ID registered in Mohali, Punjab. Yet my name has been classified as “shifted” in the draft electoral rolls.""Thankfully, these are only the Draft Electoral Rolls, not the Final Electoral Rolls. Names are corrected during the ‘Claims and Objections’ process, which is ongoing. The Final Electoral Rolls will be published in October 2026. I am already in process of availing the remedies provided under SIR guidelines," Chadha said in the post."This does not seem like a mere clerical mistake. This is a clear case of political vendetta," he added."Who marked me as ‘shifted’?An official of AAP’s Punjab Government. Who verified that classification? Again, an officer of AAP’s Punjab Government. Who processed it at higher level? Once again, the same AAP’s Punjab Government official," he said further.Chadha also alleged that officials involved in the electoral revision process were vulnerable to political pressure because their transfers and postings were controlled by the state government."From the BLO on the ground to the Chief Electoral Officer of Punjab, every operational level of this exercise is staffed by Punjab Government officials. The BLO is ordinarily a junior Punjab Government employee. The AEROs, EROs and DEOs in between are Punjab government officials. At the top is a Punjab-cadre IAS officer serving as the Chief Electoral Officer, Punjab."These officers know AAP Government controls their transfers, postings and careers once their electoral duty ends. They know who can transfer them and who can make their lives difficult. This is how the AAP government applies political pressure through state officers to execute the political revenge," Chadha claimed in the post.He further alleged that other former AAP leaders who joined the BJP had also been targeted by the Punjab government."Ever since I left the corrupt Aam Aadmi Party, its leadership has been burning with anger. It has unleashed the Punjab Police and the Punjab Government’s administrative machinery against those of us who refused to remain silent. Other MPs who left AAP and joined the BJP have also been targeted by Punjab Govt. This wrongful classification is only the latest act in that political vendetta."Chadha also cited the Election Commission’s guidelines for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.He referred specifically to Paragraph 4(d), which he said provides for a “protected list” covering public representatives, among others."More importantly, Paragraph 4(d) of the ECI’s Detailed Guidelines for SIR, create a ‘protected list’ for public representatives whose names are identified. This includes Judges, MPs and MLAs. It states:“All names of member of judiciary, public representatives, holders of declared offices and personalities from fields of arts, culture, journalism, sports, and public services etc. earlier flagged in the electoral database, are to be included in the Draft Electoral Rolls, so that necessary documents can also be collected during the period of Claims and Objections.”"I am a sitting Member of Parliament from Punjab. If at all my name was flagged, Paragraph 4(d) required my inclusion in the draft electoral rolls. The instruction was not overlooked. It was wilfully violated in my case.""AAP may run the Punjab Government, but Punjab’s Draft Electoral Rolls are not its private property," Chadha said.The AAP rejected Chadha’s allegations, saying the Punjab government had no role in deciding whose names were included or deleted from the electoral roll."Raghav Chadha has been caught by a National Daily English Newspaper, trying to get his voter registration made in Delhi through a backdated process, and is now attempting to put the entire blame on the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Punjab government.The party said the SIR exercise was conducted by the Election Commission and not the state government."SIR is conducted by the Election Commission, not the state government, so the Punjab Government has no role in deciding whose name is included or deleted from the electoral roll.It also claimed that Chadha was living in Delhi and said maintaining or shifting his voter registration was his responsibility."It is a matter of public record that Raghav Chadha has been living in Delhi and not in Punjab. If he no longer resides in Punjab, maintaining or shifting his voter registration was his own responsibility. He cannot now blame the AAP or the Punjab Government for the deletion of a voter entry.The AAP further alleged that Chadha was trying to register as a voter in Delhi’s Rajinder Nagar through a backdated process and called for an investigation."At the same time, the AAP has received information from Election Commission sources that Raghav Chadha is trying to get his voter registration made in Rajinder Nagar, Delhi, through a backdated process. If any such backdated or unlawful exercise has taken place, it must be investigated and the entire truth brought before the public.The party also said it would pursue the matter if the BJP or anyone else had facilitated an alleged backdated entry."If the BJP or anyone else has facilitated any such backdated entry, we will pursue the matter to its logical conclusion and expose the truth."The allegations come after the Election Commission published Punjab’s draft electoral roll in August as part of the second phase of the SIR exercise.Nearly 20.66 lakh voters were removed from the draft roll, accounting for 9.63% of Punjab’s 2.14 crore registered voters as of June 9, 2026.More than 1.93 crore electors, or 90.37% of registered voters, submitted forms during the 40-day house-to-house enumeration exercise held across all 117 assembly constituencies between June 25 and August 3.Of the names removed, 9,44,131 voters were classified as permanently shifted, 5,74,568 as deceased, 4,12,715 as untraceable and 1,19,145 as duplicate entries.The claims and objections process began on August 13 and will continue until September 12. The disposal of claims and objections is scheduled for October 8.
Article Summary: Raghav Chadha claims his name was marked as "shifted" in Punjab's draft electoral roll. Chadha was elected to the Rajya Sabha as an AAP nominee in 2022 and joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) this year. He claimed his voter ID was registered in Mohali and questioned why his name had been classified as “shifted”

Article Title: Dire straits: Brand on the run as Trump suggests Hormuz can be renamed in his honor
Article Text:
Trump’s latest push to rename the Strait of Hormuz adds another chapter to his growing campaign of political branding and geographic renaming

TOI correspondent from Washington:

Donald Trump has rescued a canal, invaded a country, conquered a gulf, annexed a lake -- at least on American maps -- and put his name on a performing-arts center. He now appears to have set his sights on the hottest waterway on the planet.The MAGA boss suggested on his social media account on Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz could be renamed the “Trump Strait” -- because if you cannot solve a problem, you can at least rename it.The proposal is the latest addition to what has become an extraordinary Trump-era renaming and branding binge. In January 2025, Trump ordered the Gulf of Mexico renamed the Gulf of America for US federal purposes. Last week he signed an executive order changing Lake Ontario to Lake America, saying the US had been treated badly by Canada. He then helpfully suggested that the Atlantic or Pacific could be next, saying, “We have a gulf and we have a lake…Now all we need is an ocean. ”The President, someone jibed, appears to be collecting bodies of water like refrigerator magnets.The joke became even better when Google Maps and Apple Maps fell in line.Google changed Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users over the weekend. Apple followed on Tuesday. Canadians, however, continue to see Lake Ontario and users elsewhere may see both names. In other words, the lake has acquired the geographic equivalent of dual citizenship.The tech companies' compliance prompted criticism from illuminati who argue that private corporations should not allow political pressure to dictate historical and geographic nomenclature. MapQuest, an internet relic many Americans had forgotten existed, refused to make the change and suddenly discovered the most effective marketing strategy in Silicon Valley: stand up to Trump. Its downloads reportedly surged, giving it the kind reception normally reserved for rock bands that haven’t toured for a long time or sports legends making a comeback.There is also an awkward business joke buried underneath all this. Trump built his political persona partly on branding himself as a master businessman, but his corporate record includes repeated failures and bankruptcies in hotels and casinos; His casino empire alone went through multiple Chapter 11 restructurings. Trump-branded ventures have also included products and licensing deals that did not last.Late-night television has naturally treated Trump's naming obsession as premium material. The Atlantic, meanwhile, took the joke to its logical conclusion in a satirical vision of a future America in which everything is renamed “America” or “Trump,” leaving citizens unable to distinguish between brands of products, goods, and structures.Political analysts however see a serious calculation behind what many consider trolling. The renaming campaign sure is presidential theater -- cheap to stage, impossible for the internet and tv to resist, and almost guaranteed to ignite social media. But it also serves to distract people from more pressing issues -- such as cost of living and democracy going down the tubes.
Article Summary: Trump suggested on his social media account on Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz could be renamed the “Trump Strait” The proposal is the latest addition to what has become an extraordinary Trump-era renaming and branding binge. In January 2025, Trump ordered the Gulf of Mexico renamed the Gulf Of America for US federal purposes.

Article Title: 'Stay away from Iran': US warns countries & companies as war escalates
Article Text:
Trump administration’s latest push to tighten pressure on Iran as the war escalates

US treasury secretary Scott Bessent has warned countries and businesses against supporting Iran, saying Washington is considering sanctions targeting airlines, maritime activity and digital assets as Washington expands its economic pressure campaign amid escalating hostilities.“We’re having fulsome talks with anyone supporting Iran,” Bessent said in an interview with Fox News, adding that Washington would “systematically take out bad actors.”Speaking on potential targets for further sanctions, Bessent pointed to airlines, maritime activity and digital assets, indicating that the US pressure campaign could extend beyond traditional banking and oil measures.“No one should support this regime,” he said. “My message to everyone is to stay away.”The warning comes as the Trump administration pushes its Operation Economic Outcast campaign, seeking to pressure Iran's remaining trading and financial partners to choose between doing business with Tehran and retaining access to the US financial system.The latest escalation follows a monthlong lull in fighting. Iran fired on US allies in the Gulf early Wednesday after a night of American bombardment, which Iranian officials said included a deadly strike on a wedding party.Fighting intensified after the US military struck Iranian rocket launchers on an island in the Strait of Hormuz, saying Iran planned to use them to deploy mines in the waterway. Iran retaliated with missile attacks on US bases in Jordan, which were intercepted.Iran also launched drones at Kuwait, while the UAE and Bahrain reported intercepting incoming Iranian attacks. In Iraq, Kurdish authorities said they intercepted 10 explosive-laden drones near Irbil.
Article Summary: US treasury secretary Scott Bessent warns countries and businesses against supporting Iran. He says Washington is considering sanctions targeting airlines, maritime activity and digital assets. The warning comes as the Trump administration pushes its Operation Economic Outcast campaign to pressure Iran's remaining trading and financial partners.

Article Title: Uber lays off 3,300 employees as it restructures for faster growth
Article Text:
File photo: An Uber logo is displayed at the company's headquarters in San Francisco (Picture credit: AP)

Uber seeks to cut layers and simplify teams

Only around 1% of staff to remain remote

Focus shifts towards robotaxis and AI

Uber Technologies will cut about 3,300 jobs, representing roughly 10% of its global workforce, as part of a major restructuring aimed at reducing management layers and reallocating resources towards its core ride-hailing, delivery and robotaxi businesses.The job cuts will reduce the number of managers at the company by 20%, chief executive officer Dara Khosrowshahi said in an email to employees.An Uber spokesperson said some managers would be moved into individual contributor roles, while the layoffs would also affect employees who are not managers.Uber had about 34,000 employees globally at the end of last year, according to its annual report cited by Reuters.Khosrowshahi said Uber's rapid growth over the past five years had created greater complexity within the company.“Over the last 5+ years, Uber has grown by orders of magnitude, with our top line nearly tripling,” he wrote in the email, which was obtained by Bloomberg News.“But that growth has also brought complexity: more layers, more coordination, more fragmented ownership, and in some cases structures that made sense when businesses were smaller but no longer serve us well at our current scale.”The restructuring is aimed at making the company “simpler and faster”, Khosrowshahi said.Uber has reduced roles primarily focused on coordination and broadened managers' responsibilities, particularly in teams with only one or two direct reports.According to Khosrowshahi's email, the number of employees sitting seven or more layers below the CEO has been reduced by 20%, while the number of such small teams, or “micro-teams”, has been cut by nearly 50%.The company is also combining teams where it believes fragmentation has created duplication and slowed decision-making. Uber will merge its three Delivery Operations teams covering restaurants, retail and Direct into single teams at the global, regional and country levels.Its Core Services Engineering and Science teams are also being combined, Bloomberg reported.Uber is also tightening its location and remote-work policies as part of the overhaul.The company will concentrate global teams in its largest global hubs in New York and San Francisco, while regional, local and technology teams will be based in designated hubs.The company is asking the vast majority of remote employees to move to an office. Going forward, only around 1% of Uber's employees will be allowed to work remotely, while the company will continue to enforce its hybrid policy requiring staff to work from the office three days a week.Khosrowshahi said the savings from the restructuring would be reinvested in growth, innovation and other capabilities.“Our opportunity from here is enormous: we have the chance to bring Uber to hundreds of millions more people; to invest even more in drivers, couriers and merchants; and to innovate across our core businesses and build the autonomous future,” he said.The restructuring comes as Uber has pledged to commit more than $10 billion to robotaxi partnerships in the coming years.The company has also invested in Avride Inc., Lucid Group Inc., Nuro Inc. and Rivian Automotive Inc., while reallocating capital by reducing stakes in some other companies.The latest layoffs follow more targeted job cuts Uber made this year in its customer service and human resources departments. Unlike several major technology companies, Uber had avoided large-scale workforce reductions since the Covid-19 pandemic.Uber said in May that it would moderate the pace of hiring. Wednesday's cuts will bring the company's total employee count to just under 30,000.Khosrowshahi did not mention artificial intelligence as a reason for the restructuring in his announcement, though Bloomberg reported that the changes were also being driven by Uber's efforts to use more AI technology in its daily operations.Uber's shares rose 2% following the announcement.
Article Summary: Uber will cut about 3,300 jobs, representing roughly 10% of its global workforce. The job cuts will reduce the number of managers at the company by 20%, chief executive officer Dara Khosrowshahi said in an email to employees. Only around 1% of staff will be allowed to work remotely, while the company will continue to enforce its hybrid policy.

Article Title: Oil climbs past $90 as Middle East conflict keeps Strait of Hormuz shut
Article Text:
Crude prices continue to jump as Middle East tensions intensify

Oil prices inched higher on Tuesday after renewed tensions between the US and Iran brought the risk of supply disruptions in the Middle East back to the forefront.Brent crude rose 55 cents, or 0.61%, to $91.04 while WTI crude was up 79 cents, or 0.92%, at $86.55 a barrel, around 7:30 am IST.The latest rise came after a sharp jump in the previous session. Brent ended Monday 2.7% higher, having earlier touched its strongest level since August 25. WTI settled 2.8% higher after reaching its highest since August 21.The renewed concerns followed the first direct exchange of attacks between the US and Iran in a month on Sunday. US President Donald Trump on Monday threatened further strikes against Iran, escalating tensions after the conflict had recently shifted towards an economic standoff.For oil markets, the situation around the Strait of Hormuz remains a key concern. Only five visible commodity vessels a day were seen transiting the waterway over the weekend, according to shipping data from Kpler.The strait carried about a fifth of global oil supplies before the war began in late February. Iran closed the waterway after the US and Israel attacked the country on February 28.Mediation efforts by Qatar and Oman to secure a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz have so far failed to gain traction.The continuing uncertainty around shipping was underscored on Tuesday when the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) said a tanker had reported being struck by three projectiles while sailing out of the strait. There were no casualties or environmental impact reported.Alongside the disruption risks in the Middle East, developments in Venezuela are also in focus as the US looks to replenish its oil reserves. Trump announced a deal with Venezuela on Friday to control oil reserves in the country and later said it would help replenish the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve, which is near a 44-year low.Energy companies are also moving towards agreements on projects in Venezuela. Indian oil giant ONGC, Chevron and GE Vernova of the US, Italy's Eni and Colombia's GeoPark are on track to sign final agreements after months of negotiations to firm up energy projects in the OPEC country, five sources close to the preparations said on Monday.The Strategic Petroleum Reserve itself fell further last week, with crude inventories declining by about 3.1 million barrels to 286.6 million barrels.With shipping disruptions continuing, analysts polled by Reuters in August expect oil prices to stay above $80 a barrel in 2026.
Article Summary: Brent crude rose 55 cents, or 0.61%, to $91.04 while WTI crude was up 79 cents, at $86.55 a barrel. The latest rise came after a sharp jump in the previous session. Brent ended Monday 2.7% higher, having earlier touched its strongest level since August 25.

Article Title: UAE, Egypt coordinate over Banque Misr bank after US Treasury notice on Iran links, dollar curbs
Article Text:
Egypt's Banque Misr is reviewing US sanctions targeting its UAE branches for alleged Iran dealings

The United Arab Emirates and Egyptian central banks are coordinating over Banque Misr after the US Treasury proposed cutting off the Egyptian bank’s UAE branches from dollar transactions over alleged financial links to Iran.In a joint statement on Sunday, the two central banks said Banque Misr would take “all necessary measures” to continue its business as usual, reported Reuters.The proposed US measure is expected to take effect less than 30 days after a public comment period. It applies only to Banque Misr’s UAE branches and would prevent them from carrying out transactions in US dollars through the US financial system.Banque Misr said on Saturday that it was reviewing the US Treasury notice.The move comes as Washington steps up pressure on banks and financial institutions seen as facilitating Iran’s access to the global financial system.Meanwhile, US treasury secretary Scott Bessent told Reuters on Sunday that the department was likely to announce new secondary sanctions against Iran-linked entities every week, with banks an initial focus.“You're going to see a lot more of these every week,” Bessent said, warning banks that “it’s not okay to have Iranian money and to aid the regime.”“There can be no leakage,” Bessent added, “You're either with us or you're with the Iranians.”The Treasury launched the campaign, dubbed “Operation Economic Outcast”, last week, saying it aims to cut off the financial networks that help Iran generate revenue, evade sanctions and fund its activities.This came as the US treasury alleged on Friday that Banque Misr UAE had processed about $1.8 billion for 103 companies potentially linked to Iranian shadow-banking networks between January 2024 and June 2026.The Treasury described the UAE operation as a “critical node” in Iran’s access to US dollars and said some of the bank’s customers included apparent front companies used by Iran’s Ministry of Defence and Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps to evade sanctions.The proposed rule would prohibit US financial institutions from maintaining correspondent accounts for Banque Misr UAE and require them to take steps to prevent transactions involving the UAE bank from being processed through the US financial system.The Treasury stressed that the proposed measure applies only to Banque Misr UAE and not to the bank’s operations in other countries.Bessent said the next stage of the campaign could involve cutting institutions off entirely from the dollar-based financial system, while urging G20 finance ministers and central bank governors to sever economic ties with Iran or risk secondary sanctions.The US has also imposed sanctions on Reza Mohammad Taeedi, manager of Bank Melli’s Dubai branch, and a Hong Kong-based company accused of helping sanctioned Iranian entities access the international financial system.
Article Summary: Egypt's Banque Misr is reviewing US sanctions targeting its UAE branches for alleged Iran dealings. The US Treasury proposed cutting off the Egyptian bank’s UAE branches from dollar transactions over alleged financial links to Iran.
